gaps.sentence: He apologised for ___ so rude to the waiter.
gaps.explanation: 'Apologise for being' — 'for' is a preposition, so the gerund follows.

gaps.sentence: He continued ___ as if nothing had happened.
gaps.explanation: continue takes -ing or to-infinitive. Both accepted.

gaps.sentence: I saw him ___ the wall and disappear into the garden.
gaps.explanation: see/hear + object + bare infinitive = the complete action; -ing = the action in progress. Both readings possible here; the bare infinitive is expected.

gaps.sentence: Do you want me ___ you at the station?
gaps.explanation: want + object + to-infinitive: want me to meet.

gaps.sentence: Try ___ the handle — sometimes it sticks.
gaps.explanation: try + -ing = experiment with a method; try to do = make an effort.

gaps.sentence: This new timetable will mean ___ earlier trains.
I really can't afford ___ on holiday this year.
gaps.explanation: afford takes the to-infinitive: can't afford to go.

gaps.sentence: We can't risk ___ the deadline again.
